column3: “The bearer of his armor” is rendered “the young man who was carrying his armor,” and “from the other side of this” as “on yonder side.”
“At the edge of Gibeah” is rendered “in the outskirts of Gibeah.”
“Bearing an ephod” is rendered “wearing an ephod.”
“The tooth of the rock” is rendered “a sharp crag.”
“The one tooth was a pillar” is rendered “The one crag rose.”
“There is no limitation to the LORD” is rendered “the LORD is not restrained.”
The Hebrew “turn aside for yourself” is rendered “turn yourself,” and the last “according to your heart” as “according to your desire.” The meaning of the middle phrase is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Be still” is rendered “Wait.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Answered” is rendered “hailed.”
“Was killing behind him” is rendered “put some to death after him.”
The Hebrew measure (“half a furrow, an acre of field”) is difficult; NASB renders “half a furrow in an acre of land.”
“A trembling of God” is rendered “a great trembling,” and “the destroyer” as “the raiders.”
The Hebrew ends “and it went and here”; NASB renders “they went here and there.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “was … with” to complete “the ark of God on that day and the sons of Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Was called together” is rendered “rallied,” and “panic” as “confusion.”
“As yesterday three days ago” is rendered “previously,” and NASB supplies “turned.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Passed beyond” is rendered “spread beyond.”
NASB adds “for” and renders “until the evening” as “before evening” and “and I will avenge” as “and until I have avenged.”
“All the land” is rendered “all the people of the land,” and “the surface of the field” as “the ground.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB adds “therefore,” which is not in the Hebrew.
“Certainly made to swear” is rendered “strictly put … under oath.”
